excerpt: A collection is a group of different data sources that you can search using a single endpoint.
A source connection links a specific app or database to your collection. It handles authentication and automatically syncs data.
Direct vector search. Use when speed is critical (~0.5sec).

An AI agent iteratively searches your data using tool calling. It searches with multiple strategies, reads full documents, navigates entity hierarchies (parent/child/sibling), and builds a comprehensive result set.
The Airweave MCP server implements the Model Context Protocol to let AI assistants search your synced data.
The primary use case — search any collection from your terminal

Airweave publishes official skills so that agents in Cursor, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and other environments can set up integrations and search your data without you having to explain how every time.
Airweave Connect is a hosted, embeddable UI widget that lets end users connect their apps (Slack, GitHub, Google Drive, Notion, and more) directly inside your product.
Webhooks are real-time notifications that Airweave sends when things happen in your organization: syncs completing, source connections being created, collections being updated.
Authentication providers let you reuse existing authenticated connections from third-party platforms such as Composio or Pipedream.

Airweave lets AI agents search across company knowledge bases, cloud drives, databases, and SaaS tools in a single query.

Had meetings with a ton of MCP-server providers, no one came close to Airweave’s retrieval accuracy. I even tried Zapier and similar large companies, didn’t come near airweave. Highly highly recommend if you need third party integrations to your AI agents or workflows.
Yes, a lot MCP servers are just api wrappers. Airweave looks like it copies the data and has a RAG that is processing your queries.
